newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger, 30-yr now below U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger, 30-yr now below U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, boosted by a tame U.S. retail sales report, with the Canadian 30-year bond yield making a historic move below U.S. levels, analysts said.

"Today's numbers out of the U.S. were weak. I think the market has decided it will no longer price in a significant probability of a Fed move on July 1-2. Therefore we've rallied back here," said Michael Gregory, a fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$1.72 to C$115.93 to yield 6.753 percent.

The U.S. 30-year bond rose 30/32 to yield 6.77 percent. The spread between the bonds turned negative for the first time in history, shifting from four basis points at Wednesday's close to a negative two basis points.
Analysts earlier this week predicted that Canada's growing fiscal and monetary credibility would allow the entire Canadian yield curve to trade below the U.S. curve.

"I think it's a continuation of the very good fundamentals," said Gregory. Those include a much lower inflation rate than the United States and the reduced borrowing needs of Canada's federal and provincial governments.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened this morning after the U.S. Commerce Department reported that retail sales fell 0.1 percent in May, compared with expectations of a 0.4 percent rise.
Canadian bond investors are now looking ahead to U.S. producer price index data for May due for release tomorrow for confirmation that U.S. price pressures remain subdued.
In new issue news, the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corp on Thursday set C$400 million of 5.5 percent bonds due September 3, 2002 in financial markets. The bond was priced at 98.778 to yield 5.773.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$1.25 to C$107.66 to yield 6.206 percent while the U.S. 10-year rose 22/32 to 6.48 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 27 basis points from 20 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.86 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 4.96 percent.
